findings.issue_text: [BUG] NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) but the constructor's signature is NewResourceServer(opts ResourceServerOptions) with no ctx parameter in scope at this point in the diff hunk, so the reference does not compile unless a ctx happens to be defined earlier in the function body. If no ctx binding exists above line 258, the package fails to build ('undefined: ctx'), breaking CI and every consumer of NewResourceServer; the Init-at-construction behavior is silently unreachable.

[ADVISORY] Moving Init from per-request lazy invocation into the constructor converts a per-request recoverable error into a hard construction/startup failure for the resource storage server. Operators booting Grafana with an unreachable search backing store (bleve root unwritable, backend stats query failing) now get a failed startup instead of degraded-but-serving CRUD/list endpoints; during a rolling deploy, every new pod crash-loops while old pods still serve, turning a partial degradation into a full outage window.

[ADVISORY] Reordering init so search.init (full index build) runs before initWatcher means events written between the index snapshot and watcher start are never indexed, and because init is now synchronous in the constructor, the window scales with total index build time (seconds per the logged duration_secs). Users searching for dashboards created or updated during startup get stale/missing results with no error, until the next full rebuild; previously watcher-before-search ordering minimized the gap and the lazy per-request Init provided a retry point.

[ADVISORY] The diff permanently skips the instrumentation-server integration test for postgres with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.'), removing CI coverage for the primary production database with no tracking issue reference. Regressions in the unified storage server startup path (which this same PR substantially rewires) against postgres go undetected in CI while the author's local claim remains unverified; combined with sqlite already skipped, the test now only ever runs on mysql, if any run.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock held across the entire BuildIndex body allows two concurrent calls for the same NamespacedResource key to both execute bleve.New on the same on-disk directory, and bleve's file-based index takes an exclusive lock on the directory, so the second call fails. Concurrent index builds for the same resource (possible now that init, event handling, and request-triggered getOrCreateIndex can race during startup with the new constructor-time Init) return an error from BuildIndex, causing search initialization or index refresh to fail where the old serialized path succeeded; the last-writer at line 137-141 also silently discards the other fully-built index.

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test for the storage server is now skipped in CI with only a TODO, so the changed Init-at-construction and watcher-ordering behavior in this PR has zero CI verification against postgres. Any postgres-specific regression in the resource server startup path (the exact code this PR rewrites in server.go) ships silently; the comment itself admits it fails under Drone, meaning the failure is currently unobserved and undiagnosed.

[BUG] Moving initWatcher() to run after s.search.init(ctx) creates a write-gap: changes committed to the backend while the search index is being built (which scans seconds-to-minutes of history) are never delivered to the index because the watcher is not yet subscribed. Resources created/updated during the index build window produce stale search results and stale History/Origin responses until a full reindex; previously the watcher was started first so those events were captured and applied on top of the build.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key to each construct a full bleve index; the second b.cache[key] = idx overwrites the first, orphaning the first index and any documents written to it, and both callers briefly hold different indexes. Under concurrent initial access to the same tenant/resource key (previously serialized by the lock, now only the map assignment is atomic), one goroutine indexes into an index that is subsequently discarded, so search results silently miss documents written through the losing index until a rebuild.

[ADVISORY] Calling s.Init(ctx) inside NewResourceServer converts every previously per-request recoverable initialization failure (search index build, watcher, backend priming) into a hard constructor failure, and the ctx used is whatever construction-time context was passed in — which may be short-lived or already cancelled, aborting the long index build started from it. Operators who previously got a server that served Reads/Writes even when the search index failed to initialize now get a server that refuses to start entirely; a construction ctx cancelled right after NewResourceServer returns truncates search index builds (the ctx is threaded through search.init and builders via the fix in search.go:173).

[ADVISORY] History and Origin no longer call s.Init and dereference s.search without a nil check (unlike Search, which retains `if s.search == nil`), so a server constructed without search configured panics with a nil pointer dereference on the first History/Origin request instead of returning an error. Any deployment of the resource server where the search support is optional (NewResourceServer permits s.search == nil, as Init itself guards with `if s.search != nil`) gets a runtime panic rather than a graceful error on History/Origin calls.

[ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now eagerly calls s.Init(ctx) at construction, converting what was a per-request lazy failure into a hard constructor/startup failure, a semantic change beyond the stated 'performance optimization' intent with no requirement traceability. Deployments where search-index init previously failed per-request (e.g., transient DB error building an index) now fail entire server construction, taking down the storage server process instead of degrading individual requests; operators get an unbootable Grafana where before they got errors on affected endpoints only.

[ADVISORY] The diff disables the storage-server integration test for postgres via t.Skip with a TODO and no linked issue, work not traceable to the PR's stated performance intent and not actually fixing the failure it papers over. The postgres storage path loses all integration-test coverage in CI from this PR onward; regressions in postgres storage-server behavior will land unnoticed because CI is green while the only test that exercises it silently skips.

[ADVISORY] Init() invocations were stripped from all eleven RPC handlers (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob) while the Init method itself remains exported, leaving out-of-tree ResourceServer wrappers that relied on the lazy-init-in-handler behavior (or call Init themselves) on silently changed semantics. Any embedding/wrapping code that constructs the server via a path other than NewResourceServer (or that relied on handlers self-initializing) now hits handlers with nil search/watcher state — History and Origin call s.search.History directly and panic with nil-pointer dereference since only the Search handler retains a nil check.

[ADVISORY] Widening the critical section change in BuildIndex — the b.cacheMu lock that previously serialized the entire build is now held only for the cache write — allows concurrent builds of the same key to proceed in parallel, including two bleve.New calls writing the same on-disk directory. Concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same namespace/resource during startup or cache eviction race: both run the builder, both attempt to create the same bleve file index at filepath.Join(Root, ns, resource.group), and one fails (or worse, interleaves file writes), yielding a spurious index-build error or corrupted index directory; the lock narrowing has no accompanying test demonstrating single-flight per key.

[ADVISORY] A new unconditional Info-level log line 'search index initialized' with duration and doc count is added inside init, which runs under the existing failure-timing block but is emitted even when the init path is on its retry path — instrumentation work not traceable to the performance-intent and duplicative with the IndexMetrics.IndexCreationTime metric already recorded two lines below. Operators get two parallel signals for the same event (log line + metric) that can drift; anyone adding fields to one but not the other maintains a hand-kept duplicate, and the log fires even for tenants whose index build failed partially, since it logs after the goroutine that seeds unready namespaces returns.

[BUG] Reordering search-index init before initWatcher creates a window where writes are permanently missing from the index. search.init does a full DB read to build the index, then initWatcher starts; any write committed after the index's DB snapshot but before the watcher is subscribed is never indexed (no event was observed, and the snapshot didn't include it), leaving the index stale for that document until a full rebuild or restart — search results silently omit current data.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent builds of the same key to race on the same on-disk bleve directory. Two goroutines calling getOrCreateIndex→build for the same NamespacedResource both pass the cache-miss path and both call bleve.New on the identical file dir (keyed only by namespace/resource/group); the second fails with a file-lock/lock-held error or corrupts the index, and the cache write is last-writer-wins discarding the other build's documents. The old code serialized builds precisely to prevent this.

[ADVISORY] Init is now run eagerly inside NewResourceServer using whatever context the caller passed to the constructor, turning the previously per-request lazy init into a hard startup-time failure tied to that ctx's lifetime. A caller passing a short-lived or already-cancelled request context to NewResourceServer gets a startup failure (or an index build aborted mid-way) from an operation that previously succeeded on the first real request with a fresh context; likewise any transient DB hiccup during construction now permanently prevents the server from being created where it previously only delayed the first request.

[ADVISORY] Removing the per-handler Init() calls leaves no runtime guard on s.initErr for any code path that obtains a server without going through NewResourceServer. If any test, embedding package, or alternate constructor builds the server struct directly (or a future refactor adds such a path), handlers like Search/History/Origin now dereference a nil or un-initialized s.search/diagnostics with a panic (nil pointer), where the old code returned the init error — the correctness of this diff depends solely on NewResourceServer being the sole construction path, an invariant nothing in the struct enforces.

[ADVISORY] Moving Init from lazy per-request invocation into NewResourceServer converts a previously tolerable, per-request init failure into a hard constructor failure without any explicit acceptance of that behavior change. Before this diff, a transient failure of the search index init or watcher startup (e.g. a slow backend) only failed individual requests and the server still started; now the entire resource server (and whatever embeds it, including Grafana startup paths that construct this server) refuses to start, turning a partial degradation into a full outage for operators on deploy.

[ADVISORY] Reordering initWatcher to run after search index initialization changes the server's startup semantics: events written during a long index build are no longer captured by the watcher from the start, and watcher startup is now blocked by index build duration. A tenant whose dashboard changes land during a multi-minute initial index build gets a watcher that starts late; if the search index snapshot predates those writes and the watcher missed the events, those writes are missing from search results until a rebuild. This inverts the original ordering contract (watch first, then index) that guaranteed no missed events without explicit sign-off.

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is silently skipped with a TODO comment and no linked issue, permanently dropping CI coverage for the postgres storage-server path under a PR whose changes specifically alter server startup behavior. The exact code this PR changes (eager Init in NewResourceServer) is now untested against postgres in CI — a postgres-specific init failure (the stated local/Drone discrepancy) will not be caught by the pipeline, and the skip has no forcing function to ever be reverted.

[ADVISORY] Removing the build-wide cacheMu lock from BuildIndex and holding it only around the cache write abandons the original serialization contract, allowing concurrent duplicate index builds for the same key. Two concurrent requests for the same NamespacedResource now both run the full document build and both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory when size > FileThreshold, producing a file-lock conflict error for one caller and wasted duplicate builds in memory for the rest; previously the lock guaranteed a single build per key.

[ADVISORY] The diff permanently disables the only integration test covering the instrumented resource server against postgres with an unactioned TODO skip, while simultaneously making constructor-time Init a hard startup failure that this test was the primary coverage for. CI gives a green signal for the unified storage server on postgres while the test never executes; a regression in NewResourceServer/Init on postgres (exactly the code paths this PR restructures) ships undetected. The 'works locally' comment means the failure is unexplained, not verified-fixed. Rebuttal: 'it's environment-specific' — but the diff adds risky startup-path changes in the same PR the skip lands in, so the skip masks the PR's own risk.

[ADVISORY] The new constructor-time Init error branch (return nil, err from NewResourceServer) is exercised by no test in this diff, and no existing test-file changes touch NewResourceServer. If Init fails, NewResourceServer now returns a nil server with an error; any caller that ignores the error or shares a previously-constructed server across requests gets a nil-pointer panic or a hard process startup failure where the old code served requests lazily after retry. Checked test files in diff: pkg/server/module_server_test.go (only a skip added); no test asserts the constructor-failure path. Rebuttal: 'error propagation is trivial' — but the behavioral contract changed from lazy-recoverable to fail-fast, and no test verifies either the failure return shape or that a successful construction actually initializes (search/watcher) before requests arrive.

[ADVISORY] The Init ordering change (search index now initialized before the watcher starts, previously watcher-first) has no test verifying that no write events are lost or double-indexed across the swap, and the removed per-request Init guards mean any regression here is silent. Documents written between search.init completing and initWatcher starting are never indexed (the watcher misses them, and there is no longer a lazy Init on Read/Search to paper over the gap), producing stale search results for those resources with no error. Checked test files in diff: only module_server_test.go, which asserts nothing about event/index interleaving. Rebuttal: 'events are queued by the stream layer' — no test in the diff demonstrates that, and the ordering change is precisely the kind of race that only a test with a concurrent write during Init would catch.

[ADVISORY] The BuildIndex lock is narrowed from holding cacheMu across the entire build to only the final cache write, but no test in the diff covers concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key, which the old lock was implicitly serializing. Two concurrent builders for the same NamespacedResource can now both run the expensive index build and race the b.cache[key] = idx write — last-writer-wins — so one caller indexes into an index that is immediately orphaned and a later Close/disk-dir collision on the file-backed path (same dir) can corrupt or fail. Checked test files in diff: none touch search/bleve or BuildIndex. Rebuttal: 'callers serialize above this layer' — searchSupport.build calls via getOrCreateIndex's singleflight or a mutex is not shown in this diff, and nothing tests it.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the body of BuildIndex lets concurrent builds of the same key race: two goroutines can both miss the cache check, each build a full index (one creating a new on-disk bleve index under the same directory), and the last writer to b.cache wins while the loser's index is never closed, leaking file handles and disk-backed index resources. Two simultaneous requests for the same NamespacedResource key (e.g. dashboard search warming after startup) build duplicate indexes; the overwritten index is never closed, leaking the file-based bleve directory handle, and clients can observe index inconsistency while the losing write is silently discarded with no error.

[ADVISORY] Moving Init from lazy per-request invocation to a synchronous call inside NewResourceServer converts a per-request failure into a hard startup failure with no timeout bound on the ctx passed in, so a hung backend call during search index initialization (bloom-cache size query, index build) blocks or kills the whole process startup. Operators bringing up a Grafana instance against a slow/unavailable SQL backend get a server that either never finishes constructing the resource server (unbounded hang on a context with no deadline) or refuses to start entirely, where previously the server started and individual requests failed fast with a clear error.

[ADVISORY] Reordering init so the search index builds before initWatcher starts means writes committed while the (potentially long) index build is in flight are never delivered to the watcher path that seeds incremental indexing; only whatever RV the initial build captured is present, and any write whose event fires between build completion and watcher start is permanently missing from the index with no reconciliation. Dashboards or other resources created during a slow initial index build (e.g. large tenants at startup) are silently absent from search results until the next write to that same key triggers a reindex, with no error or log indicating the gap.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

However, the claim that events in that window are *never* indexed cannot be verified from this diff alone (it depends on watcher start semantics / resource version catch-up logic not shown). The finding is still a valid, diff-grounded concern about potential missed/late indexing and reduced ability to retry init.

Since `server` is an unexported type, out-of-tree code generally cannot construct it except via `NewResourceServer`, so the claimed “constructs the server via a path other than NewResourceServer” scenario is not evidenced by this diff. Also, `History`/`Origin` already would have panicked on `s.search == nil` even before (previously they called `Init`, which does nothing when `s.search` is nil, then immediately dereferenced `s.search`). The finding’s count is also off (it lists 12 handlers but says eleven).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Widening the critical section change in BuildIndex — the b.cacheMu lock that previously serialized the entire build is now held only for the cache write — allows concurrent builds of the same key to proceed in parallel, including two bleve.New calls writing the same on-disk directory. Concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same namespace/resource during startup or cache eviction race: both run the builder, both attempt to create the same bleve file index at filepath.Join(Root, ns, resource.group), and one fails (or worse, interleaves file writes), yielding a spurious index-build error or corrupted index directory; the lock narrowing has no accompanying test demonstrating single-flight per key.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go removes holding b.cacheMu across the entire BuildIndex operation (including bleve.New/bleve.NewMemOnly and the builder callback) and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This is a concrete change that can allow concurrent BuildIndex executions for the same key to proceed in parallel if callers race, whereas previously they were globally serialized. However, the diff does not show the higher-level get-or-create logic (e.g., whether there is per-key singleflight elsewhere), so the claimed on-disk directory collision/corruption cannot be conclusively verified from the diff alone—only that the protective serialization was narrowed without any visible replacement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A new unconditional Info-level log line 'search index initialized' with duration and doc count is added inside init, which runs under the existing failure-timing block but is emitted even when the init path is on its retry path — instrumentation work not traceable to the performance-intent and duplicative with the IndexMetrics.IndexCreationTime metric already recorded two lines below. Operators get two parallel signals for the same event (log line + metric) that can drift; anyone adding fields to one but not the other maintains a hand-kept duplicate, and the log fires even for tenants whose index build failed partially, since it logs after the goroutine that seeds unready namespaces returns.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds an unconditional Info log in `searchSupport.init`:
```go
s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())
```
right before the existing `IndexMetrics.IndexCreationTime...Observe(...)` call, so there is indeed a new parallel signal (log + metric) for the same initialization event. However, parts of the finding (e.g., “retry path” and “logs after the goroutine ... returns”) are not verifiable from the shown diff; the goroutine is launched and not awaited, so the log is not after it returns. This makes it a non-bug operational/maintainability concern rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering search-index init before initWatcher creates a window where writes are permanently missing from the index. search.init does a full DB read to build the index, then initWatcher starts; any write committed after the index's DB snapshot but before the watcher is subscribed is never indexed (no event was observed, and the snapshot didn't include it), leaving the index stale for that document until a full rebuild or restart — search results silently omit current data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `server.Init`: `s.search.init(ctx)` now runs before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher started first). If the watcher is the sole mechanism that feeds post-snapshot writes into the search index, this ordering could create a gap where writes occurring after the index build starts but before the watcher subscribes aren’t observed. However, the diff doesn’t show `initWatcher()`/event replay semantics or whether writes are indexed through other paths, so the claim that documents are *permanently* missing can’t be conclusively verified from this diff alone. It is nonetheless a concrete, diff-grounded consistency risk introduced by the reordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent builds of the same key to race on the same on-disk bleve directory. Two goroutines calling getOrCreateIndex→build for the same NamespacedResource both pass the cache-miss path and both call bleve.New on the identical file dir (keyed only by namespace/resource/group); the second fails with a file-lock/lock-held error or corrupts the index, and the cache write is last-writer-wins discarding the other build's documents. The old code serialized builds precisely to prevent this.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`, `BuildIndex` previously held `b.cacheMu` for the entire function, but the diff removes that and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. The function can create an on-disk index at a deterministic directory path (`filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", key.Resource, key.Group))`) when `size > FileThreshold` with no synchronization. If `BuildIndex` is invoked concurrently for the same `key` on a cache-miss path, both goroutines can race creating/writing the same directory-based Bleve index, and the cache assignment becomes last-writer-wins. The diff itself shows the removal of the only in-function serialization that would prevent this class of race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init is now run eagerly inside NewResourceServer using whatever context the caller passed to the constructor, turning the previously per-request lazy init into a hard startup-time failure tied to that ctx's lifetime. A caller passing a short-lived or already-cancelled request context to NewResourceServer gets a startup failure (or an index build aborted mid-way) from an operation that previously succeeded on the first real request with a fresh context; likewise any transient DB hiccup during construction now permanently prevents the server from being created where it previously only delayed the first request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` before returning (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and the per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This makes initialization eager and uses the constructor’s `ctx` rather than a per-request context. While the diff doesn’t show where `ctx` in `NewResourceServer` comes from, the finding’s concern (constructor context could be short-lived/cancelled and now causes construction-time failure/aborted init) is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/architecture change worth reviewing, even if not provably a defect without seeing call sites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the per-handler Init() calls leaves no runtime guard on s.initErr for any code path that obtains a server without going through NewResourceServer. If any test, embedding package, or alternate constructor builds the server struct directly (or a future refactor adds such a path), handlers like Search/History/Origin now dereference a nil or un-initialized s.search/diagnostics with a panic (nil pointer), where the old code returned the init error — the correctness of this diff depends solely on NewResourceServer being the sole construction path, an invariant nothing in the struct enforces.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `s.Init(ctx)` calls from all RPC handlers (e.g., `Search`, `History`, `Origin`, `IsHealthy`, `Create`, etc.) and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` only inside `NewResourceServer` before returning (`err := s.Init(ctx) ... return nil, err`). This makes correct initialization dependent on callers always obtaining the implementation via `NewResourceServer`. The diff does not show any struct-level enforcement of that invariant, so constructing a `*server` via any alternate path (e.g., in-package tests/helpers) could now invoke handlers without initialization and hit nil/uninitialized fields (e.g., `s.search`, `s.diagnostics`) rather than returning an init error as before. This is a concrete robustness/architecture concern grounded in the change, but the diff alone doesn’t prove such an alternate construction path exists at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving Init from lazy per-request invocation into NewResourceServer converts a previously tolerable, per-request init failure into a hard constructor failure without any explicit acceptance of that behavior change. Before this diff, a transient failure of the search index init or watcher startup (e.g. a slow backend) only failed individual requests and the server still started; now the entire resource server (and whatever embeds it, including Grafana startup paths that construct this server) refuses to start, turning a partial degradation into a full outage for operators on deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes behavior: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), while all per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls in `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` were removed. Previously, init failures would surface on individual requests; now an init failure prevents server construction entirely. Whether this is intended isn’t shown in the diff, but the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded operational/behavior-change concern rather than a provable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Reordering initWatcher to run after search index initialization changes the server's startup semantics: events written during a long index build are no longer captured by the watcher from the start, and watcher startup is now blocked by index build duration. A tenant whose dashboard changes land during a multi-minute initial index build gets a watcher that starts late; if the search index snapshot predates those writes and the watcher missed the events, those writes are missing from search results until a rebuild. This inverts the original ordering contract (watch first, then index) that guaranteed no missed events without explicit sign-off.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly reorders initialization in `(*server).Init`: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (see `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`, moved block). Previously, the watcher was started first and the search index initialized afterward. This does change startup semantics and can delay watcher start by however long `search.init` takes; the claimed “blocked by index build duration” is directly supported by the new order. However, the stronger claim about missed events and stale search results cannot be conclusively verified from this diff alone because the diff does not show whether `initWatcher()`/the watch mechanism replays from a last-known resource version or otherwise catches up after starting. So it’s a real, diff-grounded behavioral/contract concern, but not a provable defect from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is silently skipped with a TODO comment and no linked issue, permanently dropping CI coverage for the postgres storage-server path under a PR whose changes specifically alter server startup behavior. The exact code this PR changes (eager Init in NewResourceServer) is now untested against postgres in CI — a postgres-specific init failure (the stated local/Drone discrepancy) will not be caught by the pipeline, and the skip has no forcing function to ever be reverted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a conditional skip for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with only a TODO comment and no linked issue (`t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.")`). In the same PR, the server init behavior is materially changed by eagerly calling `s.Init(ctx)` inside `NewResourceServer` and removing per-RPC `Init` calls across many methods in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`. Skipping postgres here concretely reduces CI coverage of the postgres path at the same time init semantics are altered, matching the finding’s concern. This is a real, diff-grounded review issue about test coverage/maintainability rather than a direct functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the build-wide cacheMu lock from BuildIndex and holding it only around the cache write abandons the original serialization contract, allowing concurrent duplicate index builds for the same key. Two concurrent requests for the same NamespacedResource now both run the full document build and both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory when size > FileThreshold, producing a file-lock conflict error for one caller and wasted duplicate builds in memory for the rest; previously the lock guaranteed a single build per key.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function (removed at lines ~85-90) and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end. With no other diff-shown per-key synchronization, concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` can both proceed to create/build an index. For `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`, both can call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk `dir` (`filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", ...))`), which plausibly causes file-lock/creation conflicts and duplicated work. The change therefore introduces a real concurrency/correctness regression relative to the previous serialization behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff permanently disables the only integration test covering the instrumented resource server against postgres with an unactioned TODO skip, while simultaneously making constructor-time Init a hard startup failure that this test was the primary coverage for. CI gives a green signal for the unified storage server on postgres while the test never executes; a regression in NewResourceServer/Init on postgres (exactly the code paths this PR restructures) ships undetected. The 'works locally' comment means the failure is unexplained, not verified-fixed. Rebuttal: 'it's environment-specific' — but the diff adds risky startup-path changes in the same PR the skip lands in, so the skip masks the PR's own risk.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in an integration test (`TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer`), with a TODO and "Works locally" comment, so CI will not execute that test on postgres. In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and fails construction on init errors, and the per-RPC `Init` calls are removed, which meaningfully changes startup/init behavior. While the finding’s claim that this was the *only* postgres coverage can’t be verified from the diff alone, the combination of disabling a postgres integration test and restructuring init/startup paths is a concrete, diff-grounded risk/coverage gap rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new constructor-time Init error branch (return nil, err from NewResourceServer) is exercised by no test in this diff, and no existing test-file changes touch NewResourceServer. If Init fails, NewResourceServer now returns a nil server with an error; any caller that ignores the error or shares a previously-constructed server across requests gets a nil-pointer panic or a hard process startup failure where the old code served requests lazily after retry. Checked test files in diff: pkg/server/module_server_test.go (only a skip added); no test asserts the constructor-failure path. Rebuttal: 'error propagation is trivial' — but the behavioral contract changed from lazy-recoverable to fail-fast, and no test verifies either the failure return shape or that a successful construction actually initializes (search/watcher) before requests arrive.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), while all RPC methods remove their lazy `s.Init(ctx)` calls. This is a nontrivial behavioral contract change (fail-fast at construction vs lazy init per request) and the only test change in the diff is a skip added in pkg/server/module_server_test.go; no test in the diff exercises/validates the new constructor-time error path or that init (search/watcher) happens before requests. The claim about callers ignoring errors/panicking isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the “missing test for new behavior” point is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Init ordering change (search index now initialized before the watcher starts, previously watcher-first) has no test verifying that no write events are lost or double-indexed across the swap, and the removed per-request Init guards mean any regression here is silent. Documents written between search.init completing and initWatcher starting are never indexed (the watcher misses them, and there is no longer a lazy Init on Read/Search to paper over the gap), producing stale search results for those resources with no error. Checked test files in diff: only module_server_test.go, which asserts nothing about event/index interleaving. Rebuttal: 'events are queued by the stream layer' — no test in the diff demonstrates that, and the ordering change is precisely the kind of race that only a test with a concurrent write during Init would catch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change initialization semantics in a way that could affect correctness but isn’t verifiably broken from the shown code alone. In `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`, `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` up front and the per-request `Init` guards were removed across RPCs (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). Also within `Init`, the order was changed to run `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()`. The finding’s core point—that this ordering change introduces a potential race/window and that there is no test in the diff validating event/index interleaving (only `module_server_test.go` changes, unrelated)—is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern. However, the stronger claim that documents written in that window are 'never indexed' cannot be confirmed from the diff because `initWatcher()` behavior and any catch-up/queueing semantics are not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The BuildIndex lock is narrowed from holding cacheMu across the entire build to only the final cache write, but no test in the diff covers concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key, which the old lock was implicitly serializing. Two concurrent builders for the same NamespacedResource can now both run the expensive index build and race the b.cache[key] = idx write — last-writer-wins — so one caller indexes into an index that is immediately orphaned and a later Close/disk-dir collision on the file-backed path (same dir) can corrupt or fail. Checked test files in diff: none touch search/bleve or BuildIndex. Rebuttal: 'callers serialize above this layer' — searchSupport.build calls via getOrCreateIndex's singleflight or a mutex is not shown in this diff, and nothing tests it.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex removed the b.cacheMu lock that previously serialized the whole method, and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. The diff does not show any higher-level serialization for concurrent BuildIndex calls on the same key, and no tests were added/modified to cover that concurrency behavior. While this can plausibly allow duplicate expensive builds and last-writer-wins caching (and potentially conflicting file-backed `bleve.New(dir, ...)` in the same directory), the diff alone does not prove such concurrent calls occur in practice, so it’s a concrete risk/coverage gap rather than a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the body of BuildIndex lets concurrent builds of the same key race: two goroutines can both miss the cache check, each build a full index (one creating a new on-disk bleve index under the same directory), and the last writer to b.cache wins while the loser's index is never closed, leaking file handles and disk-backed index resources. Two simultaneous requests for the same NamespacedResource key (e.g. dashboard search warming after startup) build duplicate indexes; the overwritten index is never closed, leaking the file-based bleve directory handle, and clients can observe index inconsistency while the losing write is silently discarded with no error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `BuildIndex` no longer holds `b.cacheMu` for the full duration (the top-level lock/unlock was removed) and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. That does introduce a concrete concurrency concern: if callers can invoke `BuildIndex` concurrently for the same `key`, nothing in the shown code prevents duplicate, concurrent index construction (including `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same directory) before the final cache write. However, the finding’s specific claims about an earlier “cache check” being missed and the overwritten index never being closed cannot be verified from this diff alone (the cache lookup/close logic, if any, is not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving Init from lazy per-request invocation to a synchronous call inside NewResourceServer converts a per-request failure into a hard startup failure with no timeout bound on the ctx passed in, so a hung backend call during search index initialization (bloom-cache size query, index build) blocks or kills the whole process startup. Operators bringing up a Grafana instance against a slow/unavailable SQL backend get a server that either never finishes constructing the resource server (unbounded hang on a context with no deadline) or refuses to start entirely, where previously the server started and individual requests failed fast with a clear error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization from lazy per-request calls to a synchronous call during construction: `NewResourceServer` now does `err := s.Init(ctx); ... return nil, err` and the per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from many RPCs (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This means init errors now prevent the resource server from being created at all (startup failure) rather than surfacing per-request. However, the finding’s claim that the `ctx` used in `NewResourceServer` has “no timeout bound” and could “hang unbounded” cannot be verified from the shown diff because the origin/definition of `ctx` in `NewResourceServer` is not included here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Reordering init so the search index builds before initWatcher starts means writes committed while the (potentially long) index build is in flight are never delivered to the watcher path that seeds incremental indexing; only whatever RV the initial build captured is present, and any write whose event fires between build completion and watcher start is permanently missing from the index with no reconciliation. Dashboards or other resources created during a slow initial index build (e.g. large tenants at startup) are silently absent from search results until the next write to that same key triggers a reindex, with no error or log indicating the gap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `server.Init`: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before starting the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`), whereas previously the watcher started first (see moved block around lines ~294-316). This could create an indexing consistency/race window if incremental indexing relies on watcher-delivered events that are not replayed for changes occurring during the potentially long `search.init` build. However, the diff does not show how `initWatcher()` sources events (e.g., whether it replays from a resource version or only streams new events), so the claim that writes are "permanently missing" cannot be verified solely from this patch.
